Case Name: One-click binary install brings full stack ready
Precondition:
1. One networked Linux VM (x86_64 or aarch64; Debian/Ubuntu or CentOS/RHEL/openEuler) with sudo privileges
2. The openan-installation repository is cloned and install.sh, uninstall.sh, and configure_llm.sh under binary/one-click are executable
3. The LLM configuration step is planned to be skipped (interactive input y)
Steps:
1. Run ./install.sh in binary/one-click (default --reg --orc full-stack mode; skip LLM configuration) (see Result 1)
2. Run curl http://127.0.0.1:5000/rest/v1/registry-center/agent-cards to check that registry-center is serving (see Result 2)
3. Run curl -k https://127.0.0.1/, curl -k https://127.0.0.1/registry/rest/v1/registry-center/agent-cards, and curl -k https://127.0.0.1/api/orchestrate/rest/v1/orchestrate/templates to verify the nginx single remote entry and the three reverse-proxy paths (see Result 3)
4. Cleanup: run ./uninstall.sh --force to uninstall all services (see Result 4)
Expected Result:
1. The install script exits with code 0 and the summary prints each service PID and access URL
2. Returns 200 (the binary registry-center exposes no /health route; the query API answers 200 once the service is up)
3. All three return 200 (the / path serves the frontend page; /registry/ and /api/orchestrate/ strip their prefix and proxy to ports 5000 and 5001, whose backends serve no root route)
4. After uninstall, ports 5000/5001/443 are no longer listening and the registry-center/ and orchestration-center/ directories are deleted
Notes: design method: scenario; environment: online; language_profile: shell; protocol_primitive: none; execution: smoke; verification source: binary/one-click/QUICKSTART.md service port and URL table; automation note (v0.3): binary registry-center v1.0.0 exposes no /health route and its root path serves no route; readiness is verified through the query API and the reverse-proxied API endpoints; the install summary must list a PID and URL for every started service

Case Name: Online Helm wizard install completes and platform is usable
Precondition:
1. A networked ops machine (Linux/macOS, Helm 3.14+, python3) can reach a K8s v1.25+ cluster via kubectl (nodes Ready)
2. Application images are pre-built and pullable from the image registry (available tag <IMAGE_TAG> for registry-center/orchestration-center/frontend)
3. A reachable OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint (for the wizard connectivity probe)
4. The cluster has a default StorageClass or accepts hostPath fallback
Steps:
1. Run ./install.sh in containerized/online-install with a real TTY; follow the wizard to select all components and enter image tag <IMAGE_TAG>, model configuration, initial admin password (8+ chars with upper/lowercase/digits/special chars), and PostgreSQL password; choose in-cluster postgresql for SQL hosting (see Result 1)
2. Run kubectl -n openan get pods,svc,ingress to check the deployed resources (see Result 2)
3. Open the platform home page at the Platform URL printed by the installer and call POST /api/v1/auth/token with the wizard-configured initial admin password (see Result 3)
4. On 403 Password change required: log in via POST /api/orchestrate/rest/v1/orchestrate/auth/login with the initial password, change the password via POST /api/orchestrate/rest/v1/orchestrate/auth/change-password (old_password=<INITIAL_PASSWORD>, new_password=<NEW_ADMIN_PASSWORD> meeting complexity), then call POST /api/v1/auth/token with the new password (see Result 4)
5. Cleanup: run ./uninstall.sh to remove the release and namespace resources (see Result 5)
Expected Result:
1. The installer prints the Install complete banner and the Platform access URL
2. registry-center-*, orchestration-center-*, openan-frontend-*, and openan-postgres-0 Pods are Running and Ready; Services and 3 Ingresses are all present
3. The platform home page returns 200; the first token call with the initial password returns 403 Password change required (first-boot admin must change the initial password before a token is issued)
4. The login sets a session; the password change returns success; the token call with the new password returns 200 with top-level access_token, token_type and expires_in in the response
5. helm ls -n openan is empty and no workload remains in the openan namespace
Notes: design method: scenario; environment: with-workload-cluster; language_profile: shell; protocol_primitive: none; execution: smoke; verification source: online-install/QUICKSTART.md acceptance criteria and deployment verification; automation note (v0.3): the token endpoint is reached through the ingress path /api/orchestrate/api/v1/auth/token (rewritten to /api/v1/auth/token at the OC) because the frontend gateway does not proxy /api/v1/* - product defect tracked against openan-portal and orchestration-center

Case Name: Offline compose stack installs healthy with single public entry
Precondition:
1. A networked machine has built the compose offline bundle openan-offline-compose-<TAG>.tar.gz and transferred it to the offline host
2. The offline host has Docker Engine (Compose v2.20+) and Python 3.10+ with root privileges; the default public port 8080 is free
Steps:
1. Run sudo scripts/install.sh --eval (quick evaluation mode: auto-generated keys/certificates/model config; bundled MySQL; HTTP; portal frontend) (see Result 1)
2. Run sudo docker compose -f runtime/compose.json ps to view the stack status and run curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/ to access the public entry (see Result 2)
3. Read the auto-generated initial admin password from the generated runtime env files and call POST /api/v1/auth/token via the public entry with it (see Result 3)
4. On 403 Password change required: log in and change the password via the public entry (POST /api/orchestrate/rest/v1/orchestrate/auth/login and /auth/change-password), then obtain the token with the new password (see Result 4)
5. Cleanup: run sudo scripts/uninstall.sh to stop and remove the containers (see Result 5)
Expected Result:
1. Installation completes (docker load loads images locally; compose validation passes and starts with --pull never --wait; in-container nginx -t passes)
2. registry-center, orchestration-center, nginx, portal, and the bundled database services are all healthy; the public entry returns 200
3. The first token call with the initial password returns 403 Password change required
4. The password change succeeds and the token call with the new password returns 200 with top-level access_token, token_type and expires_in
5. All containers are removed
Notes: design method: scenario; environment: offline; language_profile: shell; protocol_primitive: none; execution: smoke; verification source: offline-install-compose/QUICKSTART.md Step 5 to Step 7; automation note (v0.3): the token endpoint is reached through /api/orchestrate/api/v1/auth/token because the public nginx does not proxy the bare /api/v1/* prefix (same gateway gap as helm-online-001); after the case's own uninstall the retained SQL volume and bind-mounted data are removed so that every run is a first boot
